Status 404, Title "Task 7 not found", Detail "Resource Not Found", Instance "/api/tasks/7"

questions.prompt: Why can a `try`/`catch` around `await _next(context)` in a middleware catch an exception thrown inside a controller?
options: Because ASP.NET Core copies the exception to every middleware
Because controllers run before middleware
Because the middleware wraps everything after it, so the exception travels back up the pipeline to it
Because `_next` swallows exceptions and returns an error code
questions.explanation: Each middleware wraps the next one; `_next(context)` runs the rest of the pipeline, so an exception thrown further down propagates back into the caller's `catch`.

source.section: Custom middleware concept (example : Global exception handling) - Recommended

questions.prompt: Put the execution of a request through the global exception middleware in order when the controller throws.
steps: The controller executes and an exception occurs
The `catch` block runs and logs the error
A custom error response is returned
questions.explanation: The middleware's `try` wraps the rest of the pipeline; when the controller throws, control comes back to the middleware, whose `catch` logs and writes the response.

questions.prompt: A custom middleware class implements no interface. How does `app.UseMiddleware<GlobalExceptionMiddleware>()` know what to call?
options: By convention: a constructor taking a `RequestDelegate`, and a method named exactly `Invoke` or `InvokeAsync` that returns `Task` and takes `HttpContext` first, found with reflection
It calls the class's `ToString()` method
It requires the class to be marked `[Middleware]`
It calls every public method on the class in alphabetical order
questions.explanation: `UseMiddleware` is hard-coded to look for those exact names using reflection at startup, so no interface is needed.

questions.prompt: Why does the lesson move checks like "user must be 18+" and "email already exists" out of the controller?
options: Controllers cannot return `BadRequest`
It makes the request faster because services run in parallel
EF Core queries are not allowed in controllers
Business logic in the controller is hard to reuse and unit test and gets duplicated; a service keeps the controller thin
questions.explanation: The service enforces the rules (throwing `BusinessException` in the example), and the controller only handles the request and response.
